title: Session and login hardening, account audit log
description: Close the gaps the survey found. Store session identifiers hashed (today the raw token is the sessions primary key). Add a per-IP throttle alongside the per-username-and-IP one, so one password tried across many usernames is slowed. Add a scheduled cleanup that deletes expired sessions and old login attempts (nothing is ever deleted today). Add an account audit log covering sign-in method changes, invites, recoveries, role changes, deactivations and CLI actions, viewable by administrators. Make logout POST-only. Read the cookie name from config in internal/admin/sessions.go:70. Stop logging raw player tokens in RequireFantasyTokenAuth (middleware.go:164,170).

recommended_model.name: Opus 5.5
recommended_model.rationale: Several independent hardening changes that each need care with upgrade behaviour.

acceptance_criteria: A copy of the database does not contain usable session tokens
Existing sessions survive the upgrade or users are signed out once, cleanly - whichever is chosen is documented
Repeated failures from one IP across different usernames are throttled; throttling never lets an attacker lock a named user out of passkey sign-in
Expired sessions and login attempts older than 90 days are deleted automatically
An administrator can view the account audit log; entries cannot be edited through the UI
Logout requires POST; raw tokens no longer appear in logs

notes: The audit doc lists token entropy and player-link rate limiting as accepted by design - do not reopen them.

testing_requirements: Unit tests for throttle keys, cleanup, hashed lookup

context.user_story: As a club administrator, I want to see who changed what on accounts and know stolen backups do not contain live sessions.
context.programme: Club-readiness programme (sprints 019-024). Agreed constraints: BHPLTA clubs only; each club self-hosts its own instance; the original author must have no access to any other club's instance (no seeded accounts, no shared or default secrets, no phone-home); passkeys are the default sign-in with passwords as an optional fallback; the captain role is real; SQLite is the only supported database; CourtHive is bundled as an opt-in part of the package so clubs can run their own club championships.
